title: Victorian Santa — rebuilt base, cleaned and tidied
description: This standing Victorian-style Santa had a collapsed support — the original flimsy plastic sheet base was cracked and failing. We rebuilt a sturdy internal base, tidied the costume and fill, deep cleaned, and stood him tall again for display.
itemDetails: This freestanding Santa is an Old World / Victorian-style holiday display doll of the kind sold widely from the 1990s onward for mantel and foyer décor. Typical features are a painted character face with wire-rim glasses, a full cream curly beard and hair, a red velvet-style coat with thick cream faux-fur trim, and a floral or tapestry-pattern lining visible when the coat hangs open. Many examples stand on a fabric-covered cylindrical skirt or base that hides an internal plastic former. Accents often include faux evergreen garlands, pinecones, berries, and a small basket or gift prop. Exact maker on this piece is not confirmed from a readable label in the photos; identification is from construction and costume style. This example is a static display figure (no animation mechanism).
repairDetails: Santa arrived with the lower support failing — the original thin amber plastic sheet former under the red skirt had cracked and torn, so the costume and fill could not hold shape. We removed the damaged plastic, rebuilt a stronger curved support base to replace that flimsy sheet, tidied the batting and costume layers, deep cleaned the figure, and stitched the fabric closed over the new former so he stands evenly again.
